title: Pacing strategy patterns and performance outcomes in marathon running: A large-scale analysis of split time data
claims: The study analysed split times from 78,912 finishers of the Boston Marathon between 2015 and 2017.
Four pacing patterns were identified: even pacing 47.9%, mild positive splitting 31.9%, strong positive splitting 12.2% and variable pacing 8.0%.
Even pacing was associated with the fastest finish times; mean finish time was 217 minutes for even pacing versus 276 minutes for strong positive splitting.
Variable pacing had the highest incidence of hitting the wall, defined as a pace decline greater than 20% in the final segment, at 85.4%.
High-performance runners finishing under 3:00 showed even pacing 82.0% of the time, compared with 19.6% in casual participants.
Age and sex significantly influenced pacing strategy selection (p < 0.001).
